meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.
There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Monthly rent paid for a flat or building.

examples.trans: The rent is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alquileres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rents from the door.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Feminine: la arquitecta.

examples.trans: The architect is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arquitectos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the architects from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!
Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with preterite tense.

examples.trans: Yesterday we fixed the boiler.

examples.text: Llegué a Valencia ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I arrived in Valencia yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Tall, light home-baked cake popular for breakfast or afternoon merienda in Spain.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bizcochos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sponge cakes from the door.

meanings.note: Dolor de cabeza means 'headache'.

examples.trans: The head is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cabezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the heads from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.
Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Heating and hot-water boiler.

examples.trans: The boiler is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boilers from the door.

meanings.note: Written letter sent by post, or a restaurant menu.

examples.trans: The letter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cartas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the letters from the door.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Worn with a collared shirt.

examples.trans: The necktie is here.

examples.text: Vemos las corbatas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neckties from the door.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.
We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Official or legal paper.

examples.trans: The document is here.

examples.text: Vemos los documentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the documents from the door.

meanings.note: Dolor de cabeza = headache.

examples.trans: The pain is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dolores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pains from the door.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Multi-storey town building.

examples.trans: The building is here.

examples.text: Vemos los edificios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the buildings from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: enderecé.

examples.text: Enderezo el cuadro de la pared.
examples.trans: I straighten the picture on the wall.

examples.text: El dueño se enderezó la corbata azul.
examples.trans: El dueño straightened his blue tie.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.trans: It is a whole piece.
And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: entierro).

examples.text: El perro entierra su hueso en el jardín.

examples.text: No entierres la esperanza tan pronto.
examples.trans: Do not bury hope so soon.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?
He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Describes heritage buildings and old quarters.

examples.trans: It is a historic piece.

examples.text: ¡Un arquitecto que trabaja con patios históricos por toda Valencia!
examples.trans: An architect who works with historic courtyard buildings all over Valencia!

meanings.note: Adds an unexpected or emphatic item.

examples.text: Incluso el timbre estuvo callado hoy.
examples.trans: Even the buzzer stayed quiet today.

meanings.note: Coldest season of the year.

examples.trans: The winter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inviernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the winters from the door.

meanings.note: Stronger, more emphatic counterpart of nunca.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Plural legales.

examples.trans: It is a legal piece.

examples.text: ¡Los párrafos legales me dan dolor de cabeza incluso con dos pares de gafas!

limpiar.gloss: to clean; to polish; to wipe

meanings.en: to clean; to polish; to wipe
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Limpio el mostrador con un paño seco.
examples.trans: I wipe the counter with a dry cloth.

examples.text: Limpiamos los farolillos para la fiesta.
examples.trans: We polished the lanterns for the party.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Unit of length (diez metros) or city metro.

examples.trans: The metre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los metros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the metres from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Siento molestarle = sorry to bother you.

examples.trans: Excuse me, am I bothering you for a second?

examples.text: Aquí el ruido de los coches no molesta.
examples.trans: Here car noise does not bother anyone.

meanings.note: Plural municipales.

examples.trans: It is a municipal piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Normas municipales = city regulations.

examples.trans: The rule is here.

examples.text: Vemos las normas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rules from the door.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Esta casa tiene más de ochenta años.
examples.trans: This house is over eighty years old.
I counted eighty stone steps.

meanings.note: Plural los pares (dos pares de gafas = two pairs of glasses).

examples.trans: The pair is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pairs from the door.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pensar.

examples.trans: It is a thought-out piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Objetos perdidos = lost property.

examples.trans: It is a lost piece.

examples.text: Clara, llama enseguida a objetos perdidos de la estación.
examples.trans: Clara, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Plural principales.

examples.trans: It is a main piece.

examples.text: ¡Sí! Antes vi una segunda página sujeta detrás de la carta principal.
examples.trans: Yes! Earlier I noticed a second page clipped behind the cover letter.

meanings.note: Masculine noun of Greek origin despite ending in -a: el problema, algún problema.

examples.trans: Is there any problem with the shower?
We solve problems as a team.

meanings.note: La segunda página = page two.

examples.trans: The page is here.

examples.text: Vemos las páginas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pages from the door.

meanings.note: Written paragraph in a letter or book.

examples.trans: The paragraph is here.

examples.text: Vemos los párrafos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the paragraphs from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Llevo quince años en esta posada.
examples.trans: I have spent fifteen years at this inn.
Give me just fifteen minutes.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose blue suitcase is this?

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of romper.

examples.trans: It is a broken piece.

examples.text: Esta casa sobrevivió a ochenta inviernos y ayer a una válvula rota de la caldera.
examples.trans: This house survived eighty winters and one broken boiler valve yesterday.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

meanings.note: Estar sentado = to be sitting.

examples.trans: It is a seated piece.

examples.text: Esperen: ¿quién está sentado a diez metros en nuestro patio ahora mismo?
examples.trans: Wait—who is sitting ten metres away in our courtyard right now?

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; sobrevivir a algo = survive something.

examples.text: Este olivo sobrevivió a muchas heladas.
examples.trans: This olive tree survived many frosts.

examples.text: Mis tazas favoritas sobrevivieron al viaje.
examples.trans: My favourite cups survived the trip.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Irregular adjectival participle of sujetar.

examples.trans: It is a fastened piece.

examples.text: Espere un momento, señor: ¿ha leído la página dos sujeta debajo?
examples.trans: Wait a moment, sir—did you read page two clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Used for people working (machines use funcionar).

examples.text: Trabajo en recepción de lunes a viernes.
examples.trans: I work at the front desk Monday through Friday.
Today we all worked as a team.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El vecino vigila que la caldera funcione bien.
examples.trans: El vecino watches to make sure the boiler runs properly.

examples.text: Vigilamos la maleta hasta el mediodía.
examples.trans: We guarded the suitcase until noon.

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.
He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Válvula de latón = brass valve.

examples.trans: The valve is here.

examples.text: Vemos las válvulas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the valves from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
